theme: Steadfast love extends to the heavens, the fountain of life
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 36. It sets the darkness of the wicked heart beside the vast steadfast love of God, and it ends with the fountain of life. Read verses 5 to 9 aloud.
settingTheScene: Psalm 36 is a psalm of David, “the servant of the LORD.” It begins with a picture of the wicked person, then turns sharply to the character of God. At the center is the fountain of life: “In your light do we see light.” It sits well beside John, which says the true light has come into the world and that in him was life.
observation: “Transgression speaks to the wicked deep in his heart; there is no fear of God before his eyes” (v. 1).
“Your steadfast love, O LORD, extends to the heavens, your faithfulness to the clouds” (v. 5).
“Your righteousness is like the mountains of God; your judgments are like the great deep” (v. 6).
“How precious is your steadfast love, O God! The children of mankind take refuge in the shadow of your wings” (v. 7).
“They feast on the abundance of your house, and you give them drink from the river of your delights” (v. 8).
“For with you is the fountain of life; in your light do we see light” (v. 9).
“Oh, continue your steadfast love to those who know you, and your righteousness to the upright of heart!” (v. 10).
“There the evildoers lie fallen; they are thrust down, unable to rise” (v. 12).
interpretation:
The psalm starts in a dark place, the heart of the wicked. Sin whispers to him, and he has no fear of God. He flatters himself, so that he does not see his guilt. His words are trouble and deceit, he plots evil on his bed, and he does not reject what is wrong. The root of wickedness is forgetting God.

Then verse 5 begins with a sudden shift, like a sunrise: “Your steadfast love, O LORD, extends to the heavens.” The contrast could not be greater. The wicked heart is small and self-absorbed. God’s love reaches the sky. His faithfulness reaches the clouds. His righteousness is like the highest mountains, and his judgments are like the deepest sea. He cares for people and animals alike.

“How precious is your steadfast love, O God!” It is precious because it is a refuge: “The children of mankind take refuge in the shadow of your wings.” The image is of a bird sheltering its young. They feast on the abundance of God’s house, and he gives them drink from the river of his delights, an image drawn from Eden, whose river watered the garden.

Verse 9 is the heart: “For with you is the fountain of life; in your light do we see light.” Life is not something we have in ourselves. It flows from God. And we do not see truth by our own light but by his. Only in the light of God can we see anything rightly.

In John’s Gospel, Jesus is the fountain of life and the light. “In him was life, and the life was the light of men.” He told the woman at the well that he would give living water, and on the last day of the feast he cried, “If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink.” The psalmist’s longing is answered in Christ. The psalm ends with a prayer for continued love and protection, and with the wicked fallen, unable to rise.
connection: Genesis 2:10 describes the river of Eden. Psalm 17:8 and 57:1 use the shadow of wings. Psalm 46:4 speaks of the river whose streams make glad the city of God. Jeremiah 2:13 says Israel forsook the fountain of living waters. John 1:4, 4:14, 7:37-38, and 8:12 apply this imagery to Jesus. Revelation 22:1-5 describes the river of life and the light of God himself.
application:
Say verse 9 aloud and ask, “Where am I looking for life apart from God?”

Meditate on the size of God’s love: the heavens, the clouds, the mountains, the deep.

Take refuge under his wings. Name one worry and bring it to him.
prayerPrompts: Praise God for his steadfast love that reaches the heavens.
Tell him what it means to take refuge in the shadow of his wings.
Thank him for the fountain of life.
